t.1.6.1: The Sūta said: Then, having heard the words of Agni, O brahman, that Rākṣasa carried her off in the form of a boar, with the swiftness of mind and wind.
t.1.6.2: Then that embryo, dwelling in the womb, O upholder of the Bhṛgu lineage, fell from his mother's womb out of anger; therefore he became Cyavana.
t.1.6.3: Seeing him, radiant as the sun, fallen from his mother's womb, that demon was reduced to ashes and fell, releasing her.
t.1.6.4: Taking him up, O brahmin, the fair-hipped Pulomā, stupefied with grief, went forth carrying Cyavana Bhārgava, the delight of Bhṛgu.
t.1.6.5: Brahmā himself, the grandsire of all the worlds, saw her, the blameless wife of Bhṛgu, weeping, her eyes filled with tears. The blessed Brahmā, the grandsire, consoled his daughter-in-law.
t.1.6.6: From the drops of her tears a great river sprang forth and flowed, following the path of her, the path taken by the wife of the illustrious Bhṛgu.
t.1.6.8: Thus was Cyavana born, the mighty son of Bhṛgu. There his father saw Cyavana and that beautiful lady.
t.1.6.7: Then, seeing the river that had flowed along her path, the blessed Grandfather of the worlds gave that river its name, Vadhūsarā, near the hermitage of Cyavana.
t.1.6.9: Then Bhṛgu, enraged, asked his wife Pulomā: "By whom were you pointed out here to that Rākṣasa who wished to carry you off? For that Rākṣasa did not know you to be my wife of the lovely smile."
t.1.6.11: O blessed one, I was pointed out to that Rākṣasa by Agni; then the Rākṣasa carried me off as I cried out like a female osprey.
t.1.6.10: So tell me that, for today in my anger I wish to curse him. Who does not fear my curse, and whose transgression is this?
t.1.6.12: I, the very one, was set free by the fiery splendor of this son of yours, and that Rākṣasa, reduced to ashes, released me and fell down.
t.1.6.13: Having heard this from Pulomā, Bhṛgu, filled with the utmost fury, cursed Agni in his rage: "You shall become a devourer of all things!"
